classification.difficultyReason: Explain the equal angles and use the converse of the isosceles triangle theorem to establish three equal sides.

content.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$ opposite, all angles are equal.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with C above horizontal AB and gamma inside each vertex. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: All three interior angles are equal; no side equalities are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why all the angles are $60^\circ$.

answer.short: The three equal angles sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $180^\circ\div3=60^\circ$.
answer.worked: The interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$. Since they are equal, $\gamma=180^\circ\div3=60^\circ$.

inlines.text: Explain why the triangle is equilateral.
You have now proven a test for an equilateral triangle:
‘If all angles of a triangle are equal, then the triangle is equilateral’.

answer.short: Sides opposite equal angles are equal, so $AB=BC=CA$. Thus the triangle is equilateral.
answer.worked: Since $\angle A=\angle B$, the opposite sides satisfy $BC=AC$. Since $\angle B=\angle C$, the opposite sides satisfy $AC=AB$. Therefore $AB=BC=CA$, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.
